title: Process Capability Analysis (non-normal data with Johnson Transformation)
label1: Fits (or reuses) a Johnson transformation, transforms the data AND the specification limits, and computes the overall process capability. Within-subgroup capability (Cp, Cpk) is not computed with the Johnson transformation
variableSelcted: Select the variable (observed data, original non-normal scale) to analyze
lower: LSL - numeric value of the lower specification limit in the original scale (type NA to specify one-sided specification limits)
upper: USL - numeric value of the upper specification limit in the original scale (type NA to specify one-sided specification limits)
target: Target - an optional value specifying the target of the process (original scale)
addlSpecLines: Add additional reference lines on the plot (comma separated e.g. 0.85, 1.25)
addlSpecLinesLabel: Label for the additional reference lines (comma separated e.g. Ref 1, Ref 2)
fitJohnsonRad: Option 1: Fit the best Johnson transformation now (Z scan 0.25 to 1.25, Anderson-Darling selection)
useStoredRad: Option 2: Use the Johnson type and parameters stored with the selected variable (jtrans_* attributes, e.g. recorded via the Add/Remove Johnson Parameters dialog from a prior tranformation)
pvalueCriterion: P-Value criterion - the (fitted or stored) transformation must achieve an Anderson-Darling normality p-value above this criterion (default is 0.10)
forceTransformChk: Force the analysis even if the transformation does not meet the p-value criterion above (use with caution - the capability estimates rely on the transformed data being normal)
ichartChk: Display an Individuals (I) chart of the original data to verify process stability (capability indices are meaningless if the process is not in control)
applyC4Chk: Apply the c4 unbiasing constant to the overall standard deviation
digits: Digits - rounds to the specified number of decimal places

help.title: Johnson Capability Analysis (overall capability for non-normal data)
help.body:
Description
Performs a process capability analysis for non-normal data by first transforming the data to normality with a Johnson transformation (SB, SL, or SU family), transforming the specification limits (and target) with the same function, and then computing the overall capability indices from the normal distribution of the transformed data - the same approach when the Johnson transformation option is selected in its capability analysis

Why only overall capability (no Cp / Cpk)
If a Johnson transformation is used, within-subgroup analysis cannot be calculated and only overall capability is reported. The highly non-linear Johnson function distorts within-subgroup spread differently depending on where each subgroup lies on the curve, so a within-subgroup sigma on the transformed scale is not meaningful. If you need within (potential) capability, use the Box-Cox transformation with the standard Process Capability (Sixpack) dialog instead

How the indices are computed (both limits inside the fitted distribution range)
The specification limits are transformed: LSL* = f(LSL), USL* = f(USL). With m and s the mean and overall standard deviation of the transformed data:
Pp = (USL* - LSL*) / 6s, PPL = (m - LSL*) / 3s, PPU = (USL* - m) / 3s, Ppk = min(PPL, PPU)
Z.LSL = 3 * PPL, Z.USL = 3 * PPU, Z.Bench = Φ⁻¹(1 - p_total)
Expected overall PPM < LSL = Φ(-Z.LSL) * 1,000,000 and PPM > USL = Φ(-Z.USL) * 1,000,000. Because the Johnson function is strictly monotone, these are exact statements about the original process: P(X out of spec) = P(Y out of transformed spec). Interpret Pp/Ppk with the usual benchmarks (e.g. Ppk ≥ 1.33). Cpm is reported when both limits and a target are provided

Special handling when a specification limit is outside the fitted distribution range
An SB fit is bounded to (ε, ε + λ) and an SL fit to (ε, ∞); a specification limit outside that range cannot be transformed (log of a non-positive number). The indices then switch to the percentile method: Z1 = m - 3s, Z2 = m, Z3 = m + 3s are back-transformed with the inverse Johnson function to X1, X2, X3 in the original scale, and
Pp = (USL - LSL) / (X3 - X1), PPU = (USL - X2) / (X3 - X2), PPL = (X2 - LSL) / (X2 - X1), Ppk = min(PPU, PPL), Z.LSL = 3 * PPL, Z.USL = 3 * PPU
A limit beyond the support on the outside contributes an expected 0 PPM on that side; if the entire fitted distribution lies beyond a limit, that side is 100% nonconforming. Z.Bench is left missing when the expected total proportion is exactly 0 or 1 (it would be infinite)

Important caution: an expected 0 PPM produced this way is a model assertion, not a measurement - the SB/SL bounds are estimated from the sample and extrapolate beyond the data. The dialog prints a warning whenever this handling is triggered; treat the affected side of the capability report with skepticism and consider comparing with a non-normal distribution fit (e.g. Weibull or lognormal)

Other notes
- The analysis treats the data as individuals (no subgrouping) since only overall capability is computed
- Observed PPM values are simple counts of the original data outside the original limits
- The optional I chart (with moving-range control limits) helps verify stability first: a Johnson fit will happily "normalize" data from an unstable process and produce meaningless indices
- The capability histogram overlays the fitted Johnson density back-transformed to the original scale
